reacts_against: the polished, filtered Instagram aesthetics that followed it (2013–2020); indie sleaze's whole appeal on revival is its deliberate ugliness and flash-lit grain.
revivals: named and revived 2021–2023, largely on TikTok, as a reaction against hyper-curated influencer photography
article: Indie sleaze is unusual among internet aesthetics because almost nobody called it that while it was happening. From roughly 2006 to 2012, a loose scene around Brooklyn and East London DIY venues dressed down on purpose — skinny jeans, smudged eyeliner, a disposable-camera flash blowing out every color into the same harsh, slightly green-white — and partied in a way that got photographed obsessively by blogs like The Cobrasnake. Nobody named the look until 2021, when it resurfaced on TikTok as a reaction to a decade of ring-light influencer polish: suddenly the grainy, overexposed, color-blown photos of 2008 house parties looked like a style rather than just bad lighting. The palette isn't really a chosen one so much as the photographic signature of cheap digital flash cameras: neon accents flattened and bleached, skin tones pushed cool, shadows crushed to near-black. Because the revival is built entirely on old photos and old music rather than new designers, indie sleaze's color identity is tied unusually tightly to a specific camera technology and a specific decade, rather than to any garment or motif.
